headline: Highest risk is data leakage: dbt-core can reach a data warehouse while ai-engineering-hub has no documented isolation or egress controls, so pairwise handling of warehouse data is unsafe by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared channel is documented, and ai-engineering-hub shows no I/O surfaces or network egress, while dbt-core only calls data warehouses. A prompt-injection bridge is therefore not evidenced in default use; the main pathway would require unusual manual copy/paste or an undocumented shared workspace, so severity stays low.
conditions: IF the two agents are connected by manual copy-paste or a shared file drop, then attacker-controlled text can cross from one to the other.
IF an undocumented MCP or message queue is added between them, prompt injection risk increases.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Disable any shared clipboard or file-drop bridge.
Require human review before copying outputs between agents.
Add a provenance tag to any transferred text.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction-stripping at the handoff boundary.

B_data_leakage.rationale: dbt-core touches data warehouse data and has allowlisted network egress, so it can move sensitive warehouse content outward. ai-engineering-hub has no documented isolation or data-handling controls, and the pair lacks evidence of a safe boundary. The leakage pathway exists in default pairwise operation, though the exact data class is only partially documented.
conditions: IF dbt-core is run against a warehouse containing sensitive records, then those records can flow into its outputs or downstream calls.
IF outputs from dbt-core are copied into ai-engineering-hub without redaction, then sensitive warehouse content can be exposed.
mitigations: Restrict dbt runs to non-sensitive schemas.
Redact warehouse outputs before handoff.
Separate credentials for analytics and general-purpose tooling.
Review logs for warehouse field names and values.
requires-engineering: enforce data-class filtering at the orchestrator boundary.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: The profiles do not show overlapping write surfaces, shared filesystem access, or shared OAuth scopes. ai-engineering-hub is non-runnable with no I/O surfaces, and dbt-core only shows warehouse API calls. That makes direct write conflict unlikely; any conflict would require an undocumented shared mutable resource.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable warehouse objects, then concurrent edits can conflict.
IF an external orchestrator gives both agents write access to the same directory, then file-level conflicts become possible.
mitigations: Assign separate working directories.
Avoid concurrent writes to the same warehouse models.
Use a single writer for shared resources.
Check for overlapping credentials before execution.
requires-engineering: add locking or optimistic concurrency control.

D_cascading_error.rationale: dbt-core can act on warehouse data and produce downstream artifacts, while ai-engineering-hub is an agent/tooling repository that could be used to consume those outputs. There is no verification step documented between them, so if dbt outputs are treated as authoritative, errors can cascade into incorrect analytics or actions.
conditions: IF dbt-core outputs are fed into ai-engineering-hub prompts or workflows without validation, then incorrect transformations can propagate.
IF downstream automation trusts dbt-generated artifacts as authoritative, then a bad model change can cascade.
mitigations: Add a human review step for dbt outputs.
Validate schemas before passing artifacts onward.
Compare outputs against a known-good baseline.
Limit downstream automation to read-only consumption.
requires-engineering: add automated assertion checks between generation and use.

E_compliance.rationale: Only dbt-core is clearly tied to a regulated data class here: data warehouse data. ai-engineering-hub has no documented data classes touched, residency, or retention obligations, so a concrete compliance mismatch is not evidenced. The risk is limited to whatever warehouse data dbt processes, and the other agent is not shown to add a separate residency or retention burden.
conditions: IF the warehouse contains regulated data and dbt-core processes it under a stricter policy than the surrounding workflow, then retention or residency gaps can occur.
IF ai-engineering-hub is used to store or relay regulated outputs, then compliance scope expands.
mitigations: Classify warehouse tables before running dbt.
Exclude regulated datasets from the pair.
Review retention settings on dbt logs and artifacts.
Keep regulated outputs out of general-purpose agent prompts.
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls end-to-end.
